Building a good foundation for protection and wealth will help give you peace of mind when it comes to your future and theirs. Financial payout for death, terminal illness, and total and permanent disability. Maternity insurance if you’re growing your family. Your priority for wealth: Savings for immediate and future expenses. Retirement planning. Your priority for your dependants: Health insurance for hospitalisation. Protection against accidents, death, terminal illness, and total and permanent disability. Care plan for your parents. Contact us Protection Creating a proper safety net is critical for you and your young children. It will give you peace of mind knowing that everyone is cared for should any unfortunate events happen. What you already have1 If you are a Singaporean or PR, you’re automatically covered by three national schemes: MediSave A national savings scheme which helps CPF members save for future medical expenses, especially during retirement. MediShield Life A health insurance for large hospital bills and selected outpatient treatment costs. CareShield Life Long-term care insurance scheme for financial support and monthly cash payouts in event of severe disability. What you may consider2 Are you fully prepared for life's surprises with your current protection policies? It's crucial to ensure you have enough coverage to avoid a protection gap – when your savings, investments, and insurance fall short of covering unexpected expenses due to health issues. Here's how to find out your protection gap3: Calculate Needs: Multiply your annual income by 9 (for death) or 4 (for critical illness)2. This is what your family will need to manage without your income. Assess Resources: Add up your savings, assets, and current coverage. These are the funds available to your family. Find The Gap: Subtract the needs from the resources. If the result is negative, there's a protection gap. This means your family might struggle financially if something happens to you. National schemes do not fully cover: Hospitalisation An Integrated Shield Plan (IP) provides additional coverage for private hospitals or higher ward classes in public hospitals. Critical Illness You’ll need coverage of 4x annual income. (Recommended)4 Death & Total and Permanent Disability You’ll need coverage of 9 – 10x annual income. (Recommended)4 Maternity Coverage for baby and mum. It’s recommended to spend at most 15% of take-home pay on insurance protection. Why Act Now Health crises can cause income loss and depletion of family funds2. Ensure either partner can sustain the family if the other faces an unfortunate event. Misconceptions? Let’s correct them. Check out some common misunderstandings about financial planning and their truths. My life insurance coverage only needs to be twice my annual salary. I am young and healthy, I don’t need insurance. Health insurance is only for old people. Misconception: My life insurance coverage only needs to be twice my annual salary. Truth: In general, it’s recommended to have 9-10X your annual earnings as basic life coverage. However, this amount can vary depending on your family expenses and desired legacy, so it’s best to consult with a Financial Representative who can give you a plan that fits your needs. Source: 2022 protection gap study – Singapore, Life Insurance Association Singapore, 8 September 2023 Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: I am young and healthy, I don’t need insurance. Truth: While this is true, it is also true that health issues can arise at any time, regardless of age. It’s also wise to lock in a lower premium at a younger age.* Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: Health insurance is only for old people. Truth: Health issues and accidents can happen to anyone at any age. While older people might be more prone to certain illnesses, it's important for everyone to have health insurance. If you wait until you're older, insurers might exclude pre-existing conditions. Protect yourself by getting coverage early on. Contact us Wealth Growing your wealth gets more important when you have young children to provide for. Aside from health protection, achieving your long-term goals and securing their futures should take priority. Basics – what you should have4 Emergency Funds At least 3 – 6 months’ worth of expenses (including dependants) for rainy days. Legacy Planning A plan for a will, family trusts, life insurance, powers of attorney, and CPF nominations. What you may consider You need money to invest in your future—including retirement—and your children’s. Start planning now to give your money enough time to grow and fund these milestones. Investment It is recommended to allocate at least 10%4 of your take-home pay for key milestones. A Retirement Plan4 It is never too early to start building your nest egg for the retirement lifestyle you want, including monthly payouts. Why Act Now Supporting your dependants and lifestyle requires saving and investing early in a diverse portfolio2. As lifespans are increasing5, you’ll need a plan for your financial needs in the future. Give more time for compound interests to accumulate over the years6. Misconceptions? Let’s correct them. Check out some common misunderstandings about financial planning and their truths. Investing is risky. You need to be knowledgeable about the market to invest. I should always buy term life insurance and invest the difference. Misconception: Investing is risky. Truth: Investing does come with some risk, but there are ways to manage it. You can balance risk and potential returns by diversifying your investments and choosing lower-risk assets. Understanding your own risk tolerance and considering your financial commitments are also important in reducing investment risk. Source: Managing Investment Risk, Moneysense Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: You need to be knowledgeable about the market to invest. Truth: While investing will indeed be easier and less risky if you have at least some basic knowledge, you don’t need to be an expert in the field to start. Understanding your risk appetite, future goals, and potential risks is a good start. Speak to a Financial Representative to learn more and understand how to balance your risk appetite with your financial goals! Source: What to Ask When Buying An Investment Product, Moneysense Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: I should always buy term life insurance and invest the difference. Truth: There are pros and cons to both! While Term life insurance do charge relatively lower premiums, “investing the difference” yourself means taking on all the investment risks. It may also result in insufficient coverage in old age. Understand your financial goals, assess your situation, and talk to a Financial Representative to make the best decision for you. Contact us For Your Dependants One of the best gifts you can present to your children is securing their road ahead. What they already have1 If they are Singaporean or PR, they’re automatically covered by three national schemes: MediSave A national savings scheme which helps CPF members save for future medical expenses, especially during retirement. You can also use your MediSave to pay for medical bills incurred by your immediate family members. MediShield Life A health insurance for large hospital bills and selected outpatient treatment costs. Dependants’ Protection Scheme7 Term life insurance scheme that provides basic financial protection for you and your family in the event of death, terminal illness or total permanent disability. What they may need As children may be more prone to injuries and falling sick, it’s important to plan for comprehensive coverage for them: Integrated Shield Plan Additional coverage for private hospitals or higher ward classes in public hospitals. Life Insurance Coverage for death, terminal illness and total permanent disability. Personal Accident Coverage for injuries and accidents, including food poisoning and HFMD. Why Act Now A whole life policy builds over years, leaving a sizeable cash value8. Premiums increase with age for selected policies, your child can reap the benefits of lower premiums in the long run. Lower likelihood of pre-existing conditions excluded from your child's coverage. Misconceptions? Let’s correct them. Check out some common misunderstandings about financial planning and their truths. Maternity insurance is only for high-risk pregnancies. Only breadwinners need life insurance coverage. The policy can only be in the name of the person who buys it. Misconception: Maternity insurance is only for high-risk pregnancies. Truth: Even if you're in perfect health, any pregnancy can have unexpected complications. Maternity insurance can offer financial support during these times, helping to reduce stress and make things a little easier. Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: Only breadwinners need life insurance coverage. Truth: Life insurance can be a great support for stay-at-home parents, helping to ease financial stress around childcare and home management. It also ensures your loved ones have a secure future, leaving a legacy for your dependants if anything happens to you or your partner. Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: The policy can only be in the name of the person who buys it. Truth: Life insurance policies can be assigned to another person, to transfer its rights from one person to another. As there are several documents and processes involved, it’s best to get in touch with us to smoothen the process if an assignment is desired! You can also buy life insurance to cover someone else, provided you have an insurable interest on the insured person. For example, parents buying life insurance to cover their children or spouses buying life insurance for each other. items.full: Are you fully prepared for life's surprises with your current protection policies? It's crucial to ensure you have enough coverage to avoid a protection gap – when your savings, investments, and insurance fall short of covering unexpected expenses due to health issues.
items.path: Protection
items.text: Are you fully prepared for life's surprises with your current protection policies? It's crucial to ensure you have enough coverage to avoid a protection gap – when your savings, investments, and insurance fall short of covering unexpected expenses due to health issues.

items.full: Here's how to find out your protection gap3:
items.path: Protection
items.text: Here's how to find out your protection gap:

items.path: Protection

items.full: Calculate Needs: Multiply your annual income by 9 (for death) or 4 (for critical illness)2. This is what your family will need to manage without your income.
items.path: Protection
items.text: Multiply your annual income by 9 (for death) or 4 (for critical illness). This is what your family will need to manage without your income.

items.path: Protection
Protection

items.full: Assess Resources: Add up your savings, assets, and current coverage. These are the funds available to your family.
items.path: Protection
items.text: Add up your savings, assets, and current coverage. These are the funds available to your family.

items.path: Protection

items.full: Find The Gap: Subtract the needs from the resources.
items.path: Protection
items.text: Subtract the needs from the resources.

items.path: Protection

items.full: If the result is negative, there's a protection gap. This means your family might struggle financially if something happens to you.
